description:
AETHENOVA brings ancient Greek curiosity into modern scientific discovery.

Inspired by the pioneering work of the astronomer Hipparchus, we develop tools that make space science more accessible, transparent, and reproducible.

Our project, HIPPARCHUS, uses real NASA SPHEREx observations to explore how the infrared sky changes over time. By combining astronomical image processing, instrument-aware validation, photometric analysis, and reproducible scientific evidence, we help users distinguish meaningful changes from misleading observational effects.

HIPPARCHUS does more than compare images: it verifies whether observations are scientifically compatible, challenges its own conclusions, and explains the evidence behind every result.

Ancient Curiosity. Infinite Discovery.
summary:
HIPPARCHUS is an open-source scientific platform developed by Team AETHENOVA for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: Planet X and SPHEREx.

Using real NASA SPHEREx observations, HIPPARCHUS makes it possible to explore how the infrared sky changes over time. It retrieves astronomical images, verifies their scientific compatibility, compares observations across different epochs, and explains the evidence behind each result.

Unlike a conventional sky viewer, HIPPARCHUS checks wavelengths, detector quality, astrometric alignment, and measurement uncertainties before interpreting apparent changes. Its Discovery Stability Fingerprint evaluates whether conclusions remain reliable under alternative analysis settings.

Our real-data demonstrations include measured variability in RW Aurigae, a justified rejection of saturated observations of Barnard's Star, and an analysis of WISE 0855 with no significant detected variability.

The platform establishes a reproducible scientific foundation for future investigations of faint and moving objects, including Planet X candidates.

**Observe. Verify. Challenge. Explain.**
details:
HIPPARCHUS ~ The Universe Is Never Still

Team AETHENOVA | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 | Planet X and SPHEREx

The Problem

NASA's SPHEREx mission observes the infrared sky across multiple wavelengths and epochs, creating opportunities to study astronomical variability and investigate moving objects.

However, comparing astronomical images is scientifically challenging. Changes in wavelength, detector response, saturation, background emission, image alignment, and measurement uncertainty can create apparent differences that are not genuine astrophysical changes.

We developed HIPPARCHUS to help users investigate these observations while understanding which conclusions the data actually support.

Our Solution

HIPPARCHUS is an open-source astronomical exploration and scientific validation platform built around four principles:

OBSERVE → VERIFY → CHALLENGE → EXPLAIN

Observe: We retrieve genuine SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 observations from NASA/IPAC IRSA and present their images, coordinates, wavelengths, and observation dates.

Verify: We evaluate detector quality flags, wavelength compatibility, WCS alignment, saturation, and uncertainty before interpreting differences between observations.

Challenge: We compare scientifically compatible epochs, perform photometric measurements, inspect control sources, and test the stability of our conclusions under different analysis parameters.

Explain: We provide scientifically interpretable results, explicit rejection reasons, uncertainty information, and reproducible evidence linked to the original NASA observations.

Real Scientific Results

We evaluated three astronomical targets using genuine SPHEREx data.

RW Aurigae: We measured substantial variability, with a flux ratio of approximately 2.56 in a selected compatible epoch pair. The result is supported by sensitivity checks and comparisons with reference sources. We explicitly acknowledge that the SPHEREx measurements include unresolved contributions from the binary system.

Barnard's Star: Our system rejected unsuitable saturated and flagged observations instead of producing an unreliable measurement.

WISE 0855−0714: We found no statistically significant variability above our detection threshold in the evaluated observation pairs. We distinguish this result from proof that the object is intrinsically constant.

These demonstrations validate aspects of our scientific workflow. We do not claim to have discovered Planet X or a previously unknown astronomical object.

Scientific Innovation

Our central contribution is an evidence-driven astronomical comparison workflow.

The Discovery Stability Fingerprint tests whether a conclusion survives reasonable changes in photometric apertures, background estimation, masking, calibration, and observation compatibility rules.

We also developed an experimental ePSF-based photometric method to independently examine measurements from the existing aperture-photometry pipeline.

Evidence records preserve observation identifiers, source references, processing settings, checksums, measurements, and limitations.

Planet X and SPHEREx

SPHEREx provides repeated infrared observations that can support investigations of faint objects and changes in sky position.

HIPPARCHUS currently establishes the foundations needed for scientifically valid multi-epoch comparisons. Extensions toward moving-object candidate searches, astrometric tracklets, and motion-aware source verification are areas of ongoing development.

We distinguish implemented capabilities from experimental and future research.

Technology and Impact

Our scientific backend uses Python, FastAPI, Astropy, NumPy, SciPy, and astronomical image-processing libraries. The frontend uses React and TypeScript.

We use NASA/IPAC IRSA observations, with relevant astronomical catalogue information from Gaia and SIMBAD.

The project includes automated validation, reproducible scientific evidence, a public Judge Mode, technical documentation, and scientific reporting.

HIPPARCHUS aims to make infrared astronomical research more accessible to students, researchers, educators, and citizen scientists without sacrificing scientific rigor.

Ancient Curiosity. Infinite Discovery.
